body:
Greg's direction (2026-10-17 17:44Z, relayed by Engram::Advisor, TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #997), quoted verbatim:

"Greg's direction: do not spend further capacity trying to attribute the 20 s admission stall with more small synthetic benchmarks. He directly observes seconds of 100% NVMe and host unresponsiveness. Treat host disk saturation as a real operating condition: retain the current concrete typed-busy fix, prioritize production-size/host telemetry only when it informs a fix, and schedule/backpressure heavy gates so they do not overlap destructively. Continue independent correctness work; do not present the quiet-slot benchmark as evidence that the incident is absent."

COORDINATOR RULE (Fable2), derived from this:
- In any shared window, at most 3 cargo builds run at once, and at most 1 of them COLD (fresh target).
- Never start a cold build while a full gate runs, from either project.
- Stagger GOs, and wait for one run's END before the next cold GO.
- Prefer warm roots.
- The registration timeouts (w-b37b) and Engram busy/locked errors are consistent with this disk saturation; don't attribute them further with benchmarks.

AGREED with Engram::Fable (ebe242f7 #2641 and Fable2's reply), superseding the cap above:
- at most 3 concurrent cargo or npm build processes across BOTH projects;
- cold compiles one at a time across both projects;
- TermAl at most 2 concurrent, Engram at most 2, staggered;
- full gates strictly serial;
- mail Engram before any TermAl cold start.
